transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

It can take up to a day for your fridge freezer to recover if a door was left ajar or if you have put a large amount of warm food inside. Please allow some time for the temperature to stabilise naturally. Has a door been left open or not shut properly recently, or has a lot of warm food gone in?
Not that I know of - the doors have been shutting fine and nothing warm went in. It's been about 5 days of the fridge being at 10C now, so I don't think it's just settling.

Thanks for letting us know about the doors staying shut. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is around 3–5°C and the freezer at -18°C, while also confirming that no holiday or eco mode is active. You can refer to the picture shown in the app for guidance on locating these settings. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

The dial inside is on 3 out of 5, so I think that's normal. There's no display, just the dial, and I can't see any eco or holiday mode. Fridge thermometer says 10C and the freezer is around -16C. No burning smell or tripping, but I can hear it running a lot.

Thanks for letting us know about the fan noise. Cold air enters through vents, usually on the back wall inside. Please ensure food isn’t pressed against them and that shelves aren’t packed so tightly that air can’t move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
I can't see any vent in the fridge part, so not sure what I'm looking for. Nothing is packed tight against the back as far as I can tell. Should I be looking somewhere specific?

Please run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Just look and feel along the rubber — don't pull or cut it. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
Had a feel round both doors - the rubber looks fine to me, no splits or gaps and nothing folded. The fridge door closes and the cabinet door moves with it.

[Heading: Blocked vents / over-packing]
Thanks for confirming the door seal is fine. Based on our checks so far, the most likely issue is blocked vents or over-packing in the fridge freezer. It is also possible that there is an issue with the sealed cooling system or its controls. The check for this is simple; please inspect these areas and let me know what you find if it doesn't sort the problem out.

I've already checked the vents as best I can and can't see any in the fridge part. The plinth grille at the bottom isn't blocked. Is there anything else I can try? I can't pull it out as it's screwed into the cabinet.

[Heading: Sealed cooling system]
Thanks for the update on the vents and coils. Based on what you have described, the sealed cooling system or its controls is the most likely area of concern, though I cannot confirm this from our current information, nor can I attribute it to the compressor alone. Please do not open any pipes or covers; a refrigeration engineer is the necessary next step, and I am not recommending any parts at this stage. In the meantime, keep the doors shut. Chilled food that has been warmer than 8°C for more than about four hours is safest thrown away, and thawed food should not be refrozen unless it is cooked first.
